course_name_original: Técnicas de Inspección y Análisis no Destructivo

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to use different inspection techniques based on non-destructive testing methods and to interpret the records obtained.
Ability to decide which inspection process or processes are most appropriate to apply in each particular situation.
Ability to design inspections and handle the equipment to be used in them.
Ability to evaluate and interpret the results of inspections performed using non-destructive testing.
Ability to accept or reject the piece under examination according to the applicable regulations in each case.
Understand the fundamental processes used for non-destructive testing.
Understand the operational techniques and limitations of each of these inspection tests.
Understand the most characteristic defects that can appear in pieces obtained using different manufacturing methods.
Understand how to interpret the indications obtained after performing the various inspection tests.
Understand the existing regulations for accepting or rejecting the inspected piece or structure.
Understand how to carry out the qualification of personnel for performing inspections using non-destructive testing.
Definition of the most appropriate inspection system for each particular case.
Handling of technical specifications and available regulations on inspection using non-destructive testing.
Ability to adequately interpret the results of inspections performed.
Use the different available techniques in combination to obtain detailed information on the materials under study and solve practical problems that may arise.
Encourage in the student a concern for the acquisition of practical knowledge.
Lay the foundations for the student to be able to apply the acquired knowledge in engineering.
Formation of an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Quality control and introduction to non-destructive testing: Nature and application of non-destructive testing. Basic stages of inspection. Economic factors.
Visual inspection: General aspects. Personnel qualification. Detectable defects. Evaluation of defects.
Liquid penetrant inspection: Materials and equipment. Inspection process. Acceptance criteria.
Magnetic particle inspection: Fundamentals of the method. Magnetization systems. Magnetic particles. Demagnetization. Interpretation of indications. Acceptance criteria.

Radiographic inspection using X-rays and gamma rays: Radiation sources. Procedures and operating techniques. Geometric factors. Exposure factors. Sensitivity and image quality. Discontinuities. Acceptance level.
Ultrasonic inspection techniques: Equipment and ultrasonic waves. Reflection, transmission, and attenuation. Calibration. Operating techniques. Applicable regulations.
Other inspection techniques: Eddy currents. Acoustic emission. Holographic interferometry. TOFD techniques.
Personnel qualification: Qualification levels. Candidate requirements. Qualification examinations. Certification and renewal.
teaching_methods: External internships (in other institutions or companies)

assessment_methods.method: Reports of group work, presentation and debate
Execution of exercises and resolution of practical cases

assessment_rules: The overall assessment of laboratory practice reports accounts for 10% of the final grade. The group work reports, along with their presentation and debate, account for another 20%. The remaining 70% comes from two final tests: a written test on theoretical content (40%) and a practical test involving exercises and case studies (30%). A minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required in the combined evaluation of these two final tests to pass the subject.
